A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPO/MSPO research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and four pages of supplementary material. All 14 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original SD-1.5 and SDXL evaluations, ablations, a human preference study and generated-image examples, including supplementary examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–9, the user study in Figure 6 and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The written SPO objective in Eq. (5) changes timestep sampling from U[1,T] to U[1,T−κ]. This is a limited objective revision; SPM architecture, candidate pairing, random selection and MSPO remain. The conflicting retained t≤κ description prevents inferring a corresponding implementation change.

E1.justification: Pick-a-Pic training and validation, GenEval, PartiPrompts/HPSV2 user evaluation and graphic-design transfer are retained. Table 3's GenBench-to-GenEval correction and Glyph-SDXL's renaming to Glyph-ByT5-SDXL identify existing evaluations rather than new coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator memberships remain unchanged in the corresponding experiments: Tables 1–3 retain their vanilla models, Diffusion-DPO, MAPO, DDPO and D3PO where previously evaluated. DDPO remains in Table 2 despite the shortened prose list. Table 5 retains the same named SPM variants.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 changes the reported SPM ablation setting: v2 specifies removing timestep conditioning and using uniform noise sampling for all steps, whereas v3 specifies only removing conditioning. This revises the reported protocol without establishing a rerun. Main splits, metrics, training budgets and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The SPM ablation is recast as a test of timestep conditioning alone, dropping the accompanying uniform-noise intervention described in v2. Table 5's evidence remains unchanged. The other ablations in Tables 4–9 and supplementary disagreement case studies are retained without new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores and user-study percentages without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The supplementary material adds no uncertainty reporting in either version.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their numerical entries, Figure 6 retains its preference percentages, and computational-cost figures and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, SPO-SDXL's aesthetic score remains 6.364 and its GenEval overall score remains 55.20. The explicit text-preservation statement reiterates Figure 7's existing content-accuracy finding.

T1.justification: Eq. (5)'s change from U[1,T] to U[1,T−κ] alters the mathematical domain of the aggregated loss; it is not equivalent notation. Other equations and supplementary modulation formulas remain unchanged. The revised endpoint is not reconciled with the retained t≤κ rule and [0,750] experimental range.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed reason for faster convergence from stepwise alignment of fine visual details to more accurate SPM preference labels; the introduction adds this explanation too. The central contributions concerning aesthetic alignment from generic preferences, SPO/MSPO and training efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds preference-label accuracy to its causal explanation of convergence speed, without adding a label-accuracy experiment. Existing interpretations of image-text alignment tradeoffs and limitations concerning flow-matching models, subjective aesthetics and crowd-sourced preferences remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 removes the explicit uniform-noise sampling detail for the SPM ablation. PickScore initialization newly mentioned in Section 4.2 was already documented in v2's supplementary Section 2. Hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, detailed prompts and code/model access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The same 35 cited works and the positioning against trajectory-level preference optimization remain. Glyph-ByT5-SDXL refers to the same work already cited as reference 14; the expanded name does not introduce a new research relationship.

P1.justification: Scattered copyedits standardize generic-preference terminology, correct grammar and clarify training and sampling explanations. Author affiliations and contact information are revised, and acknowledgments are added. The main narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains clearer row labels but becomes a lower-resolution composite, visibly reducing fine detail when enlarged. Figure 5 and Table 1 are repositioned, and several captions are corrected, including Tables 2–3. The same figures, tables and displayed examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves terminology, caption accuracy and sampling explanations, but Figure 2 loses fine detail relevant to assessing aesthetics. Eq. (5) changes its timestep range without resolving the mismatch with the retained cutoff description. With unchanged empirical evidence, these clarity gains and visual and mathematical drawbacks leave the net quality effect uncertain.
